agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: Persistent repo instructions should be short, local, and enforceable.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: Agent context files can make agents explore more and obey local rules, but unnecessary requirements add cost and can reduce task success.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: Put the full research shelf in generated artifacts and docs; keep AGENTS.md to the rules future agents must actually follow.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: Every nontrivial coding task needs an executable verification loop.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: Agents improve when they can run tests, compare expected outputs, or validate artifacts themselves.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: Add scripts/artifact checks for new lanes and wire them into npm run check:all before committing.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: Read the repo shape, make the smallest useful plan, then code.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: Agent failures cluster around broad changes, wrong assumptions, and poor local context.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: Use rg and nearby patterns first; for large changes, state the file set and gates before editing.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: Prefer coherent implementation units that a strong engineer could review in one sitting.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: Large multi-file PRs are riskier for agents, while tiny unrelated commits create overhead.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: Group commits by artifact lane: fixture, builder, generated artifact, docs, and checks.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: State transitions and external IO need inspectable logs, artifacts, or evidence records.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: AI agents under-handle logging and post-generation log repair without deterministic guardrails.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: For wallet, submit, indexer, oracle, and custody work, output reviewable artifacts with endpoint, network, txid, payload, status, and rollback fields.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: Do not invent private company agent practices.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: Some high-performing company workflows are private, internal, or only partially described in public docs.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: Record public examples and empirical findings; mark unknown company practices as unknown instead of treating blog summaries as universal truth.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: Good agent instructions name concrete files, commands, conventions, and traps.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: Public repo examples and instruction-format guidance converge on actionable local context rather than vague best-practice prose.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: Prefer 'run npm run check:all' and 'do not use REST submit for payload receipts' over broad rules like 'be careful' or 'write high quality code'.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: Crypto product code is reviewed around value flow and adversarial failure modes, not just happy-path type checks.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: Top engineers identify custody, ordering, oracle, rollback, and abuse paths before naming a product done.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: Every app lane must name funds held, signer authority, wrong/stale data behavior, replay/rollback behavior, and user-visible failure state.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: When the user says continue, keep moving through concrete queued tasks until stop, pause, or a real blocker.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: Repeated permission checks waste the user's time and break long-running implementation flow.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: Use MEMORY.md and npm run project:queue to choose the next task; update handoff notes after meaningful work.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: A feature is code plus behavior, not a label or standalone fixture.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: Planning artifacts only matter when they drive a command, validate a boundary, or narrow the next implementation step.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: Each feature should have an input or event source, state transition, user/operator review surface, validation gate, and handoff note.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: Prefer fewer stronger verticals over more app labels.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: The repo is strongest when wallet, indexer, custody, attestation, and proof rails get deeper instead of spreading into shallow lanes.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: New app ideas should reuse an existing rail or remain research until the first executable artifact and boundary exist.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: Before extending code, check whether the surrounding code already contains a bad assumption.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: Research on buggy-code completion shows code models often continue from buggy context instead of stopping to repair the premise.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: For wallet, indexer, custody, and submit code, inspect the nearest existing reducer, artifact, and negative test before adding a sibling path.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: Review AI patches against known LLM bug classes.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: Empirical bug taxonomies include misinterpretation, missing corner cases, wrong types, hallucinated objects or attributes, incomplete generation, and prompt-biased code.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: Check every new builder for input shape, absent fields, empty arrays, duplicate rows, stale state, wrong network, and generated names that do not exist.

agentOperatingPrinciples.principle: A green happy-path check is not a security review.
agentOperatingPrinciples.why: Secure-coding benchmarks and Copilot studies show generated code can pass functional expectations while preserving insecure behavior.
agentOperatingPrinciples.repoPractice: Secret handling, shell execution, payload preservation, wallet submit, rollback, and external endpoint code need negative checks or explicit review artifacts.

kaspaDailyQaThemes.theme: Base of Liquidity can frame Kaspa's asset role, but it is not itself an app, use case, or adoption strategy.
kaspaDailyQaThemes.repoRule: Do not let BoL language replace concrete product rails, on-chain usage, or app-market evidence.

kaspaDailyQaThemes.theme: Generic real-world merchant or point-of-sale payments were explicitly down-ranked as the adoption battle for 2026.
kaspaDailyQaThemes.repoRule: Keep invoice, receipt, payload, and wallet work because they are necessary rails, but do not market generic POS payments as the main killer app.

kaspaDailyQaThemes.theme: Coordination markets are the founder-highlighted new product category, while copying useful apps from other chains still requires business development.
kaspaDailyQaThemes.repoRule: Move coordination-market research and product rails higher in planning, while keeping the current toy prototype clearly below Staghunt/Hashdag production claims.

kaspaDailyQaThemes.theme: Narrative-setting matters, but a hook without product or interesting on-chain activity wastes attention.
kaspaDailyQaThemes.repoRule: Optimize work order for usable artifacts, accepted state, and measurable app activity before broad marketing copy.

kaspaDailyQaThemes.theme: The issue is lack of a unified narrative more than lack of a unified voice.
kaspaDailyQaThemes.repoRule: Keep README, docs, generated artifacts, UI, and Kaspa Explained copy aligned around the same lanes and boundaries.

kaspaDailyQaThemes.theme: Small covenant apps can launch after the hard fork; serious means potential for real usage, and the bottleneck is business development as much as technology.
kaspaDailyQaThemes.repoRule: Treat post-HF app plans as product-readiness work, not only compiler or proof work.

kaspaDailyQaThemes.theme: The stated direction is L1-first and not EVM/L2-led; external L2s can fragment messaging, standards, and network effects.
kaspaDailyQaThemes.repoRule: Do not make EVM compatibility or external L2 dependency a default assumption for TN12, Kaspa Explained, or roadmap artifacts.

kaspaDailyQaThemes.theme: Real adoption should be visible in clear on-chain metrics, while much of crypto remains ghost-chain or synthetic activity.
kaspaDailyQaThemes.repoRule: Distinguish real accepted activity, repeated useful app use, liquidity, and durable users from demos, mints, campaign traffic, or price attention.

kaspaDailyQaThemes.theme: Universal scheduler research and netsplit resistance/100 BPS are important but not current product claims.
kaspaDailyQaThemes.repoRule: Track them as research/watch items; do not fold them into current TN12 app readiness.

failureModes.risk: AI states roadmap or testnet behavior as current mainnet fact.
failureModes.guardrail: Require status lane: live mainnet, TN12/Toccata, roadmap, research, or local artifact.

failureModes.risk: AI invents wallet/RPC/kaspa-wasm methods or wrong transaction field names.
failureModes.guardrail: Check implementation docs/source and run a local adapter/dry-run check before claiming the surface exists.

failureModes.risk: AI adds generic rules until future agents spend tokens obeying stale or irrelevant instructions.
failureModes.guardrail: Keep repo AGENTS.md short and executable; store longer research context in docs/artifacts reached only when relevant.

failureModes.risk: AI touches many files without a coherent review unit, increasing missed regressions and CI failures.
failureModes.guardrail: Use one lane per commit and make checks prove fixture, source, generated artifact, and docs moved together.

failureModes.risk: AI treats fixture replay, planner state, or signed drafts as accepted custody or network proof.
failureModes.guardrail: Positive app-state transitions need accepted TN12 tx evidence; custody claims need amount-matched accepted outputs and spend authority.

failureModes.risk: AI says DEX, lending, perps, bridge, or stable-value is buildable without reserves, custody, oracle, liquidation, settlement, and ordering rails.
failureModes.guardrail: Run missing-rails and research-trigger artifacts before upgrading any DeFi/product claim.

failureModes.risk: AI writes code that works locally but weakens secret handling, shell execution, payload preservation, replay safety, or submit permissions.
failureModes.guardrail: No secret serialization, no default broadcast, no shelling untrusted input, exact transaction preservation, rollback guard, and negative tests.

failureModes.risk: AI writes vague or hype copy that sounds confident but fails a beginner/source check.
failureModes.guardrail: Use concrete-first language, cite sources, and keep every claim tied to what a user can inspect now.

failureModes.risk: AI turns payment speed, invoice receipts, or merchant tooling into the headline adoption thesis.
failureModes.guardrail: Describe payment/payload work as rails and proof surfaces; prioritize coordination markets, useful app activity, and visible on-chain metrics for adoption language.

failureModes.risk: AI imports the Ethereum rollup/EVM mental model and treats Kaspa app strategy as external L2 migration.
failureModes.guardrail: Use the L1-first lane unless a source explicitly describes a compatible bridge/runtime experiment; keep ecosystem L2 references as research or app-surface scouting.

failureModes.risk: AI changes too much surface area and hides behavioral regressions under cleanup.
failureModes.guardrail: Use focused commits, local gates, and explicit diff review; leave unrelated churn alone.

failureModes.risk: AI broadcasts, pushes, deletes, or connects to external systems without a human review boundary.
failureModes.guardrail: Broadcast remains explicit; wallet connector run is dry-run until a real wallet and user action exist.

failureModes.risk: Many lanes, fixtures, and generated artifacts make a small proof kernel look like a product suite.
failureModes.guardrail: Lead public copy with accepted txids, scripts, and SDK lessons; keep lane count and research surfaces secondary.

failureModes.risk: A script that reads JSON and emits JSON is treated like product progress even when it adds no new evidence.
failureModes.guardrail: A fixture transform counts only if it catches a bug, tightens a claim, exposes a missing rail, or drives the next accepted transaction.

failureModes.risk: Words like app, market, DeFi, stable-value, agent, and coordination make research or planner state sound implemented.
failureModes.guardrail: Keep those terms research/planner-labeled until custody, settlement, wallet, indexer, and failure paths exist.

failureModes.risk: Every page repeats all non-claims, making the repo read like machine-generated scaffolding.
failureModes.guardrail: Put boundaries once in the right artifact and keep public-facing copy short: what landed, how to verify, what broke, what is next.

failureModes.risk: Code treats a transaction id as one spendable pledge, missing that distinct outputs in the same transaction are different UTXOs.
failureModes.guardrail: Key custody, import, and matching logic by full outpoint: txid plus output index.

failureModes.risk: AI extends an existing wrong assumption because nearby code or prose looks authoritative.
failureModes.guardrail: Before extending a pattern, verify the pattern against source docs, accepted evidence, local negative tests, and the current status lane.

failureModes.risk: AI references a field, file, package script, wallet method, or artifact row that sounds consistent but is absent or shaped differently.
failureModes.guardrail: Use rg, schema/artifact inspection, and check assertions before naming fields or wiring generated artifacts.

failureModes.risk: AI handles the normal row while missing duplicate txids, empty arrays, stale signals, wrong network, missing payload bytes, rollback, or mutually exclusive UTXO spends.
failureModes.guardrail: Add negative or review cases for duplicates, absent txids, stale rows, payload mismatch, rollback, and spent-output conflicts.

failureModes.risk: AI treats passing local checks as proof that secret handling, wallet submit, endpoint IO, or public copy is safe.
failureModes.guardrail: Pair green checks with explicit security/status review where the change touches secrets, signing, submit, indexing, external data, or user-facing claims.

topCryptoEngineerRules: State the asset/custody model before building the product model.
Separate transaction acceptance, payload event state, custody, spend authority, and user-facing readiness.
Treat oracles as adversarial inputs with stale, wrong, delayed, manipulated, and unavailable modes.
Design rollback/reorg/replay behavior before claiming indexer-derived app state.
Prefer small auditable state machines over broad magical abstractions.
Make every unsafe action explicit: signing, broadcasting, importing outpoints, upgrading claims, and changing source status.
Prove negative paths or document why they still need fresh expendable outputs.
Never rely on model memory for current protocol status when primary docs/code or accepted transaction evidence can be checked.
When copying ideas from other chains, copy jobs-to-be-done and failure lessons, not protocol claims.
Before a DeFi claim, name reserves, LP shares, custody, oracle, liquidation, settlement, ordering/MEV, and bridge/source-chain anchors.
Treat payment, invoice, and accepted-payload work as base rails unless the product has repeat usage, liquidity, distribution, and a reason users care beyond speed.
Make coordination-market and real-time-decentralization research concrete before promoting it: who commits, what is measured, how settlement happens, and what can be inspected on-chain.

requiredRepoAudits.question: Does every claim say whether it is accepted TN12 proof, accepted payload/indexer state, wallet policy, planner state, roadmap, or research?
Do wallet, RPC, payload, and transaction APIs match docs/source and local executable checks?
Does any lane imply funds moved when it only has a payload/planner event?
Could a reader mistake roadmap/vision language for current production behavior?
Have Yonatan/Hashdag, Michael Sutton, Kaspa docs, Rusty Kaspa, Silverscript, and Kaspa Daily Part 2 been checked recently?

operatingRules: Do not let AI memory upgrade a claim; primary docs, source code, accepted transaction evidence, or explicit artifact status must do it.
When a source is not accessible, record that boundary and ask for pasted/exported content instead of summarizing unseen text.
Treat AI-written code as untrusted until local checks, negative checks, and source/API verification pass.
Keep persistent agent instructions concrete and short; push longer rationale into docs and generated artifacts.
For crypto apps, write the custody/oracle/ordering/finality model before product language.
Treat generic merchant payments as rails, not the main 2026 adoption vector, unless a source and artifact prove product pull.
Keep coordination-market direction high-priority but status-labeled until opacity, capital multiplexing, and settlement rails exist.
Default to Kaspa L1-first language; do not import EVM/L2 assumptions without a specific sourced reason.
For Kaspa Explained, prefer concrete source-backed explanations over broad future-facing claims.
For TN12, keep signed drafts, planner payloads, accepted payload events, accepted proof spends, and custody outputs separate.
